cool_rest_note — removed on audit: The record opens: 'After the bloom period, cut back and reduce watering until the foliage dies back...' but neither cited quote (NC State's dormancy passage or Clemson's '2 to 4 months in dry soil' line) contains 'cut back' at all. I fetched NC State's full page text, which shows these are two separate, sequential steps for two different purposes: 'It will bloom in the spring after which cut the leaves back to the first two leaves to encourage a second bloom. After the second bloom reduce watering until the foliage dies back.' Cutting back is a mid-season pruning technique done after the FIRST bloom specifically to force a SECOND bloom cycle; only after that second bloom does the plant enter the dormancy sequence of reduced watering and natural die-back (no pruning involved at that stage). By splicing 'cut back' onto the front of the dormancy instructions, the record's note implies pruning is how dormancy is initiated, inverting the source's actual sequence and could mislead a reader into pruning at the wrong point or skipping the second-bloom step entirely.

records.name_note: Also commonly called blue wing flower or bluewings; the "wishbone" name comes from the two stamens inside the flower joining at the tip in a wishbone shape.
unknowns: No admissible source addresses toxicity of Torenia fournieri to cats, dogs, or any other animal (checked NC State, Clemson HGIC's dedicated pet-safe and poisonous-houseplant lists, RHS, and Missouri Botanical Garden). toxic_to_pets was left null rather than inferred as safe or unsafe.

Clemson HGIC's 'Wishbone Flower' page actually covers two distinct plant types under one common name: a seedless trailing hybrid type referred to only generically as 'Torenia' (not identified to species) and a compact upright type explicitly identified as Torenia fournieri. Care details given only for the trailing type -- e.g., 'Use a liquid fertilizer every two weeks' and its 'heat and humidity' tolerance -- were NOT attributed to fournieri specifically and were excluded from this record to avoid misattributing hybrid-specific care to the species; only the paragraph explicitly labeled '(Torenia fournieri)' was used.

RHS rates Torenia fournieri Hardiness 'H2' ('tolerant of low temperatures, but not surviving being frozen (1 to 5)' degrees C) but this is a UK hardiness-scale label, not an explicit Fahrenheit chill-damage threshold or a stated frost-kill temperature, so chill_damage_f and day/night F fields were left null rather than converted or guessed.
RHS lists soil pH tolerance simply as 'Acid or Alkaline or Neutral,' which signals broad tolerance but does not resolve to a specific numeric pH range, so soil_ph_min/soil_ph_max were left null.

No admissible source gives explicit numeric values for direct sun hours, humidity percentage, light foot-candles, fertilizer interval/strength, or water check depth/growing-dormant day counts for Torenia fournieri -- only qualitative guidance (e.g., 'morning sun and afternoon shade,' 'slow-release fertilizer,' 'consistently moist'), so these fields were left null rather than estimated.

RHS lists 'Full sun, Partial shade' as this species' Position in UK gardens, while US-based sources (NC State, Clemson, Missouri Botanical Garden) consistently emphasize part shade to full shade and note it dislikes hot afternoon sun in warmer climates; full_sun is included in outdoor_sun_exposure on RHS's authority but likely reflects cooler UK growing conditions rather than hot US summers.

Missouri Botanical Garden lists USDA Zone '2 to 11' for this plant, reflecting that it is grown as a warm-season annual almost everywhere (not overwintered outdoors); this was not used to derive Fahrenheit temperature fields since it is a hardiness-zone range, not a stated temperature.

outdoor_sun_exposure — removed on audit: The list includes 'full_sun', sourced only to RHS's Position field, verified verbatim on the live RHS page as 'Full sun, Partial shade'. But the other three dedicated-species/genus sources -- all US-based and all independently verified verbatim -- consistently place this plant in shade-leaning conditions and explicitly warn against strong direct sun: MOBOT's Sun field says 'Part shade to full shade' and its Culture text (verified live) says the species 'is not terribly fond of hot and humid summer weather' and 'needs protection from the hot afternoon sun'; NC State's Light tags list only Dappled Sunlight/Deep shade/Partial Shade (no full-sun option) and its description says 'It prefers part sun to shade, especially in hot summer climates'; Clemson's dedicated Torenia fournieri (compact type) passage says 'plant them outdoors in part to full shade' and 'most flowering occurs in locations with morning sun and afternoon shade.' Three separate dedicated-species US authorities contradict full_sun as a safe exposure for this plant, while only a UK source (where summer sun intensity/heat differs materially from the US) lists it. The record's own unknowns entry acknowledges this tension but does not resolve it -- full_sun remains in the list despite being the minority, geographically-caveated view, creating real risk that a US user would site the plant in sun that the weight of evidence says will scorch/stress it. This value should be dropped or explicitly scoped to UK/cool-summer conditions rather than presented as a blanket-applicable exposure.
